title: File for your residence permit within 8 working days
whatHappens: The clock starts the moment you land. Italian law requires you to apply for your *permesso di soggiorno* (residence permit) within 8 working days of arrival. You fill in a form from the yellow *Kit Giallo*, available at post offices with a *Sportello Amico* counter, and pay around €116 in fees.
whoDecides: The Questura (immigration police) reviews and issues the permit; the post office just handles the paperwork.
timing: 8 working days from landing — the strictest deadline in the entire process.
whatCanGoWrong: Missing this window, or using the wrong post office, delays everything that depends on it: your fiscal code, your bank account, your residence.
whatKimereDoes: We tell you exactly which post office to use, help you fill in the Kit Giallo correctly, and make sure you don't lose a single one of those 8 days.
